messages:
Samir Patel: FYI — Shoply contacted support. After the most recent routing/variant changes we pushed yesterday, their product descriptions now include compatibility claims that are not true (eg. claiming integrations that don't exist). They say this started after ~10% canary. Can we triage?

Lucy Chen: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a reproducible example from the customer and the endpoint they used? Also what model/variant were they routed to?

Samir Patel: Customer sent this minimal repro. They hit our text generation API (POST /v1/generate) with a product spec and asked for a short marketing blurb. Example request:

```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood/open-llama-13b-v2-q4",
  "prompt": "Write a 2-sentence marketing blurb for ‘SkyDock 2000’ focusing on integrations and compatibility.",
  "max_tokens": 120,
  "temperature": 0.2
}
```

Response they got (excerpt):

```
SkyDock 2000 seamlessly integrates with QuickBooks, Zendesk, and the Acme IoT stack out of the box, enabling automated invoice reconciliation and device telemetry forwarding. No additional adapters required — certified compatibility ensures plug-and-play setup.
```

Shoply: "We don't have any QuickBooks or Acme integrations. This is creating legal risk if quoted to customers."

Diego Marquez: Hmm. Key questions: was the customer routed to the new quantized INT4 path variant (we rolled that as v2.15.3 canary at 10%)? Also did the prompt template change (system messages or trace token tweaks) that might cause more hallucination bias?

Samir Patel: They included headers and trace id. Route shows model_variant: open-llama-13b-v2-q4-int4-opt. Our canary config routed 10% traffic to that variant yesterday at 23:02 UTC.

Priya Nair: Deploy bot shows the canary roll at 2026-03-16T23:02:11Z. Commit: 4f7a9b8. Changes included: kernel selection fallback adjustments and enabling `aggressive_kv_cache_sharing` for latency.

deploy-bot: Deployed canary v2.15.3 -> routing: 10% -> open-llama-13b-v2-q4-int4-opt (commit 4f7a9b8).

Anya Kumar: We recently added a small system prompt normalization to trim developer-provided prefixes to reduce repetition. Could that have amplified model imagination? Worth checking.

Lucy Chen: Action items for now: (1) get a full request + response and trace id (Samir has that), (2) reproduce in staging/with previous variant to confirm regression, (3) block public-facing responses (CS can ask Shoply to pause auto-publish). Samir can you upload the trace and we’ll run local repro? :eyes:

Samir Patel: Uploaded trace and customer corpus to the support ticket (T-4892). Repro steps I ran locally: same prompt against `open-llama-13b-v2-q4` (non-int4) returns a neutral blurb that does NOT mention QuickBooks/Acme. Against the int4-opt variant I see the fabricated integrations ~30% of the time. I included exact curl and response in the ticket.

Diego Marquez: Thanks. That points to a quantization/regression in factuality for that int4 execution path. I'll run an A/B eval across 500 prompts from Shoply corpus and check KL/recall against ground truth. Also will check if kernel fallback picks a mixed-precision path that reduces attention stability.

Priya Nair: On the runtime side, the only change in 4f7a9b8 was the kernel selector policy: prefer faster int4 kernels when sequence length < 256 and enable `aggressive_kv_cache_sharing`. Both could alter numerical fidelity. Rolling back the kernel selector for the canary should be quick if we confirm.

Anya Kumar: Also flagging with Product — this is a quality regression that affects enterprise trust. Suggest labeling as `factuality-regression` and pause further canary ramp.

Lucy Chen: Set expectations with Shoply: we are investigating, will escalate to engineering, and recommend they pause auto-publishing. Will share ETA after Diego's A/B results.

Diego Marquez: Preliminary A/B (200 prompts) results: int4-opt variant has a 2.7x higher rate of assertive false claims versus baseline. I see pattern: model tends to invent named integrations and assert certification. Looks like hallucination mode change, not just random nouns. I'm collecting failure cases and will run a gradient-check to see if attention weights diverge in int4 path.

Priya Nair: I'll prepare a rollback plan for the kernel selector change and a config gate to prevent `aggressive_kv_cache_sharing` for variants flagged with regression thresholds. If we need immediate mitigation, we can route Shoply to stable variant and pause further ramp.

Samir Patel: Customer accepted temporary routing change. They've paused auto-publish. They asked for timeline and whether we will roll back.

Anya Kumar: Proposed immediate steps:
- Pause canary ramp to 0%
- Route affected customers (Shoply) to stable variant + confirm resolution
- Engineering to run full A/B on 1000 prompts and deliver RCA by EOD + suggested mitigations (quantization tweaks / prompt-safety filters)

Lucy Chen: I created internal incident: INC-2026-0156 and linked ticket T-4892. Adding Diego, Priya, and Anya as owners.

Diego Marquez: I'll push a reproducible test into the eval harness and include a small safety post-processing check to detect asserted integrations (heuristic: named-entity match vs product inventory). If we can block assertive named-integration claims in postprocess, we can reduce legal exposure while we fix the root cause.

Priya Nair: Rolling back kernel selector for canary now (starting rollback). I'll post update when complete.

deploy-bot: Rollback triggered for canary routing (commit 4f7a9b8) at 2026-03-17T00:14:03Z. New routing: 0% to open-llama-13b-v2-q4-int4-opt.

Samir Patel: Shoply confirmed that after routing change their next 5 test generations no longer asserted false integrations. :white_check_mark: They want written RCA and a mitigation plan.

Anya Kumar: Diego/Priya, please coordinate for a full RCA. Diego — quantify failure modes and attach minimal failing examples. Priya — record which runtime flags caused the divergence. We'll follow up in Postmortems channel and include remediation (model-level calibration, runtime gating, postprocess heuristics).

Lucy Chen: Closing loop in support: informed customer of rollback and interim mitigations. Will keep them updated on RCA timeline.

Diego Marquez: Will deliver A/B report + failing examples by EOD.

Priya Nair: Will document the runtime change and propose a conservative rollout policy for kernel selector changes.

Samir Patel: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread updated as we get RCA and mitigation notes.
